title: AO/550/2017 of THE ORIENTAL INSURANCE CO. LTD Vs SMT. CHINTA RAWAT

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Appeal from Order No. 550 of 2017
The Oriental Insurance Com. Ltd. ... Appellant
Vs.
Smt. Chinta Rawat and others ... Respondents
Advocates : Mr. M.K. Goyal, Advocate, for the appellant
 Mr. Nikhil Singhal, Advocate, for the respondents.
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
The claimants/respondents, on 11.12.2015, had instituted a
MACP Case No. 179 of 2015, Smt. Chinta Rawat & other Vs.
Shri Dildaar Singh & others, by invoking provisions contained
under Section 140, to be read with Section 166, of the Motor
Vehicles Act, 1988, for the grant of adequate compensation, on
account of the death of one Mr. Rajesh Rawat, who is said to
have met with sad demise due to the accident, which had chanced
on 27.11.2015.
2. The claimants in the claim petition have come up with the
case, that on the date of accident i.e. on 27.11.2015, at about 7.00
p.m., while the deceased late Mr. Rajesh Rawat, was returning on
his motorcycle, bearing registration No. UP83K8491, to his
residence, after performing of his official duties, when he reached
near Village Daulatpur, a Truck, bearing registration No.
UK04CA 4967, which was said to have been driven rashly and
negligently by the driver of the vehicle i.e. opposite party No. 3,
to the claim petition, had dashed against the motorcycle resulting
into sufferance of grievous injuries on the body of the deceased,
due to which later on he succumbed to the injuries and later on,
the claim petition was filed by the claimants of the deceased, i.e.
wife, children and the mother of the deceased.

2
3. It was contended by the claimants in the claim petition
that the deceased and the claimants were the residents of
Green Vally, Suman Vihar, Bahadarabad, Haridwar and on
account of ill fated accident, which had chanced on
27.11.2015, due to collision of the two vehicles i.e. Truck
belonging to opposite party No. 1, which was being driven by
opposite party No. 3, which dashed against the Pulsar
motorcycle, which was being driven by the deceased late Mr.
Rajesh Rawat, and since the deceased, at the time of the
accident was working as a Supervisor in Jaishree Polymer
Pvt. Ltd. Begumpur, Bahadarabad, it was contended by the
claimants that the deceased was drawing a salary of Rs.
28,663/- and there was a possibility of future enhancement in
the service benefits and the future prospect too, which was
also one of the aspects, which was required to be considered.
4. It was contended by the claimants, that as a
consequence of the occurrence of the ill-fated accident on
27.11.2015, an FIR was also registered as Case Crime No.
167 of 2015 under Sections 279, 304A IPC. The post mortem
was conducted on the corpus of the deceased and it was
reported therein that the death was caused on account of the
injuries suffered due to the accident. Accordingly, the
claimants, based on the salary which was accruing to the
deceased, had raised a claim of Rs. 38,00,000/-, which was
allegedly claimed to be payable to them on account of the
dependency.

3
5. The claim petition was contested by the Insurance
Company appellant herein, and they have filed their written
statement being paper No. 29B on 16.03.2016, and in the
pleadings, thus taken therein in the written statement, the
only ground, which could be said to be tenable, which could
have been established by the Insurance Company, was
pertaining to the annual income of the deceased, as pleaded
by the claimants in para 3 of the written statement and
secondly, pertaining to the validity of the documents of the
offending vehicle i.e. Truck having been driven by the driver,
in order to shift the burden of payment of compensation on
the owner of the vehicle. The learned counsel for the
appellant further submitted that the Insurance Company
reserves its right under Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles
Act for proceeding accordingly.
6. The claimants, before the learned Motor Accidents
Claims Tribunal, in support of their contention, had appeared
in the witness box and had recorded their statements as PW1
and PW2. Apart from that, they had also produced PW3 Mr.
Arvind and had also produced and examined the
documentary evidences i.e. paper No. 9C i.e. copy of the
FIR, Paper No. 9C2, the tahrir report, the driving license,
copy of the registration certificate of the vehicle i.e. the
offending Truck, which had been involved in the accident,
the Insurance Cover Note, the post mortem report being
paper No. 13C2 and the death certificate of the deceased late
Mr. Rajesh Rawat, and in order to show the age of the
deceased, the claimants had also placed on record the

4
AADHAAR Card of the claimant No. 1, Smt. Chinta Rawat
and the copy of the birth certificate of other claimants,
including the proof of age of the deceased.
7. Apart from above, they have also filed document by
way of list paper No. 43C2, and paper No. 44C2 i.e. the copy
of the FIR and the site plan, the post-mortem report paper
No. 44C9 and 5 other documents and particularly, the
documents, which would be of much relevance for
consideration of the present Appeal from Order, qua the
document which had been submitted by way of list paper No.
49C and 50C i.e. the salary slip of the deceased for the month
of August, September and October, 2015. Apart from it,
claimants have also placed on record the salary statement of
the deceased and the copy of the document paper No. 50C1
i.e. Form-16 of the deceased, in order to show that the salary,
which was accruing to the deceased for the period from
01.04.2015 to 27.11.2015.
8. Based upon the aforesaid pleadings, and oral evidences,
what is important here to be remarked is, that apart from
filing the written statement by the Insurance Company, in
fact, the Insurance Company has not endeavoured to produce
any oral statement, nor any documentary evidence was filed
by the them, to prove to the contrary, the fact of the income
accruing to the deceased, which was attempted to be
established by the claimants by placing on record the salary
slip paper No. 50C1/3. In fact, a very vague assertion was
made by the Insurance Company/ appellant, herein in their

5
written statement, that the monthly salary, which has been
shown as to be Rs. 28,663/- accruing to the deceased; was a
false statement, but no attempt was ever made by the
insurance company, to elaborate on the stand taken by them
in the written statement by producing any documentary or
oral evidence to the contrary, to denounce the claim of the
claimants as substantiated by them by leading evidence on
record.
9. Based on the aforesaid pleading, the learned Motor
Accidents Claims Tribunal, vide its order dated 31.08.2016,
had framed the following issues:-

10. What is important to be remarked herein at this juncture
itself is, that while formulation of the issues on 31.08.2016,
which have been extracted above, it has been observed by the
learned Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, that none of the
parties to the claim proceedings, before the learned trial
Court, had ever made any efforts to call upon the learned
Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal for formulation of any
other additional issue, to be answered based on the pleadings

6
and the evidences, which have been led by the parties to the
proceedings.
11. The learned Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, while
answering to the issues, which have been framed before the
learned Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal and particularly,
with regard to the establishment of the factum of accident
and the death having been caused to the deceased late Mr.
Rajesh Rawat, due to the injury suffered by him on account
of the accident were the admitted fact, apart from being
established by documents evidence.
12. The learned Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, had
placed reliance upon the charge sheet, the site plan, which
had been prepared by the Police Authorities, about the
accident, which has chanced on 25th November 2015, and
also the documents on record in order to establish the
involvement of the two vehicles in the accident. But, in case
if the finding recorded by Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal
on issue No. 1, is taken into consideration, there is nothing on
record or any finding which has been recorded, to the effect
that the accident was caused as a consequence of a
'contributory negligence', which has been sought to be
argued by the learned counsel for the insurance company, for
the first time before this Court contending thereof, that since
there were two vehicles which were involved in the accident,
due to which the deceased had suffered injuries and as there
was a head of collision the case would be that of a
contributory negligence.

7
13. The aspect pertaining to the contributory negligence
may not be invariably irrespective of the circumstances of the
case, irrespective of the case pleaded in the written statement
and irrespective of an issue, being derived, before the learned
trial Court, for getting a finding returned on it as to whether
the accident was as a consequence of a contributory
negligence, it may not automatically always lead, to an
inference that whenever the two vehicles are involved in an
accident, it would be deemed, even without appreciation of
evidence to be led by the parties, that it was as a consequence
of a contributory negligence, because this Court is of the
view that a fact of contributory negligence, the benefit of
which would have always accrued to the insurance company
or shifting of burden of payment of compensation to the
insurance company is a fact, which is required to be
established by the parties to the proceedings, who is trying to
derive the benefit out of it and in the instant case, particularly
since it is a plea, which has been raised by the insurance
company before this Court, for the first time, the learned
counsel for the insurance company was called upon to show
as to whether the plea of contributory negligence, ever
constituted as to be part of the pleading in the written
statement or it was ever attempted by the appellant, before
the learned Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, to get an issue
formulated on the same.
14. On appreciation of the evidence and particularly, the
pleading of the written statement, I am of the view that since

8
the appellant had never established or ventured to establish
the fact of contributory negligence, by raising a plea in the
written statement, and obviously there could not have been
any evidence to be led with, to establish a fact of contributory
negligence, without there being a prior pleading existing in
the written statement, because the aspect of contributory
negligence would always, be related to the establishment of
the fact, which was required to be discharged by either of the
rival parties, who wanted to shift the burden of meeting the
liability of compensation, as a consequence of the accident,
which has chanced on 27th November 2015, and that is what
has been observed by the learned trial Court, also while
framing the issues. That part from the issues, which have
been extracted above, no other issue was attempted to be
framed by any of the parties to the proceedings, including the
insurance company nor any evidence was attempted to be led
to the contrary on the same, hence the plea of contributory
negligence raised by the learned counsel for the insurance
company for the first time before this appellate Court is
answered against him and he cannot take the liberty to plead
the same for the first time at an appellate stage and that too,
without even making an attempt to modulate or amend the
pleadings of the written statement or getting an issue framed
by this Court even while exercising its powers under Order
41 Rule 25, to get a finding returned from the trial Court on
the issue of contributory negligence, which would be always
based upon the establishment and appreciation of evidence.

9
15. When the appellant has not attempted to invoke Order
41 Rule 25 C.P.C., in order to get an issue framed on an
aspect of contributory negligence, they had pleaded that the
liability cannot be harnessed exclusively on the insurance
company on the pretext of a contributory negligence is a fact
which doesn't stand established and this argument of the
learned counsel for the appellant is not acceptable by this
Court.
16. The learned trial Court had framed the second issue,
which related to, as to whether on the date of the accident,
the offending vehicle was being driven under a valid licence
or not, the learned Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, while
considering the contents of paper No. 10C, that was driving
licence of the Truck driver i.e. opposite party No. 3, to the
proceedings; as well as which scrutinising the validity of the
licence, which was held to be valid upto 23rd December,
2029 and the manner in which the accident had chanced, as
would be apparent from the findings recorded therein since
the vehicle was found to be validly driven under the valid
licence including a valid insurance cover note, which was
valid for the period from 26.02.2015 to 25.02.2016, it was
rightly held by the tribunal, that the vehicle was indeed being
driven under a valid document, and hence the insurance
company would be liable to meet the liability of
compensation, which was to be determined by the learned
Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, while deciding issue No.
3, with regard to the proportionality of adequacy of the
compensation to be paid to the claimants.

10
17. In fact, there is no Cross Appeal or any other
independent Appeal from Order, which has been filed by the
claimants, seeking enhancement of the compensation, which
has been otherwise determined by the learned Motor
Accidents Claims Tribunal, to be made payable to them to
the tune of Rs. 32,61,000/-, the division of which has been
given in the operative portion of the judgement, which has
been made entitled to be paid to the claimants on the ratio as
settled therein.
18. Let us revert back to the logic, which has been assigned
by the learned Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, while
determining the compensation and applying the multiplier
based upon the age of the deceased on the date of the
accident. The learned Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
while determining the age of the deceased, the learned
Tribunal, has made reference to the PAN Card which had
been issued by the Income Tax Department, to the deceased,
where his date of birth was recorded as to be 01.01.1974 and
also his date of birth which was recorded in the Aadhaar
Card, that too was recorded as 01.01.74, hence learned Motor
Accidents Claims Tribunal, based on the date of birth of the
deceased, which was recorded in the official document,
which could be taken into consideration by way of an
evidence in any other judicial proceedings, particularly, the
Aadhaar Card, has rightly arrived to a conclusion that on the
date of the accident, the deceased was of 41 years 10 months

11
of age, and hence the compensation was to be determined on
the basis of the established age of the deceased.
19. The learned Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, on the
aspect of the income, which was accruing to the deceased,
which was a fact attempted to be denied, though without any
material basis, the Insurance Company had submitted in their
written statement that the income, which was depicted, was
not a correct income, which was reflected therein as per the
pleadings raised in para 3 of the written statement, has been
established to the contrary against them by learned Motor
Accidents Claims Tribunal, when the Tribunal has recorded
its finding based on the statement, which had been recorded
by PW1 Smt. Chinta Rawat, and PW3 Arvind, who was also
an employee of the said factory where the deceased was
working and were the independent witnesses, who had
established the fact that the deceased was earning a sum of
Rs. 28,663/- and even the witnesses have also proved the
salary bills, which was placed on record by way of
documentary evidences, for the month of August, September
and October 2015 and more particularly, the salary
certificate, which has been issued by the employer, i.e. paper
No. 50C2, which showed that the gross salary, which was
accruing to the deceased was Rs. 28,663/- and take home
salary of the deceased, after making the relevant admissible
deductions from the salary, was assessed to be Rs. 27,383/-.
20. The learned Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, in order
to determine the annual dependency while rounding of the

12
figures of the take home salary, which was deduced by the
Tribunal to be Rs. 27,383/- has rounded it off and had arrived
at the conclusion that the salary accruing to the deceased was
Rs. 28,663/- and hence the annual dependency was assessed
to be Rs. 3,36,000/- and after making the relevant deductions
of 1/3rd amount i.e. equivalent to Rs. 1,12,000/- had
determined the total annual dependency of 2/3rd of the salary,
accruing to the deceased, which was assessed to be Rs.
2,24,000/-.
21. Hence, on the basis of the documentary evidence and
oral evidence, which was adduced by the claimants which
were based on the salary certificate and the statement of the
witnesses particularly, that of PW3, who was a co-employee
of the same factory, in which the deceased was employed, the
factum of income accruing to the deceased of Rs. 28,663/-
was and would be an un-rebutted evidence, which stood
established before the learned Motor Accidents Claims
Tribunal and thus by applying the multiplier of '12', the
determination of the annual income, accruing to the deceased
as to be Rs. 3,33,000/- was rightly arrived at.
22. The aspect with regard to the applicability of multiplier,
as per opinion of this Court, would always be depending
upon the age of the deceased. In the instant case, the finding
recorded in para 13 of the impugned award, the
determination of the age, which has been arrived at by the
learned Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, as to be of 41
years 10 months, is based upon a rightful appreciation of a

13
public document i.e. Pan Card and the Aadhaar Card, which
are the widely and publicly accepted documents, which could
be read in evidence in any judicial proceedings, to establish
the contents of the fact, which has been given in the aforesaid
two documents. Hence, the conclusion drawn that the age of
the deceased on the date of the accident was 41 years 10
months, would yet again be a fact, which stood established
beyond doubt and the applicability of multiplier, based on the
determination of age as to be multiplier of '14', was rightly
assessed by the learned Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
arriving to a conclusion that the total award, which the
claimants would be entitled to receive, as to be Rs.
32,61,000/- based on which the classification of the
remittance of the amount to the respective dependents has
been made in the operative portion of the impugned award.
23. The learned counsel for the Insurance Company, before
this Appellate Court, had submitted that the allowances
which constituted to be the part of the salary, which was
proved by the salary bills, i.e. paper No. 50C2, was inclusive
of the allowances, which was accruing to the deceased and
his argument was from the perspective that the allowances,
which had accrued to the deceased on account of his
employment, ought not to have constituted, as to be an
income accruing to him, in order to determine the
dependency. This Court is of the view, that the allowances,
which are payable to an employee as a consequence of his
engagement into the services, or the financial benefits which
accrues in a monetary terms for the services rendered by an

14
employee in his official engagement, it will constitute as to
be the part of his earning and when it constitutes to be a part
of his earning and it is a financial benefit accruing to the
deceased employee, it will be treated as to be a part of the
salary and the parameter for determination of dependency
after inclusion of the same cannot be said to be arbitrary or
contrary to law in any manner, whatsoever, and more
particularly, when even this aspect, which has been attempted
to be argued by the learned counsel for the appellant before
this Court, was not an issue which was ever raised in the
written statement nor was a pleading which was pressed into
at the time when the claim petition itself was being argued
before the learned Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal.
24. In view of the applicability of multiplier of '14', and
the dependency, which has been determined and for the
reasons which has been recorded above, this Court is of the
view, that the principles adopted by the learned Motor
Accidents Claims Tribunal, would fell well within the ambit
of the judicial parameters of an adequate determination of
compensation under the provisions of Motor Vehicles Act,
hence the award doesn't suffered from any apparent error of
facts and law, as such, which would call for any interference
by this Court.
25. Accordingly, the Appeal from Order stands dismissed.
The learned Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, before whom
the amount of Rs. 16.00 lakh has been directed to be
deposited by the interim order dated 8th November 2017,

15
after adjustment of the amount, which has been directed to be
withdrawn by the appellant by the interim orders of this
Court, would be deducted from the actual awarded amount
and the balance amount would be remitted to the appellant.
As far as the statutory deposit of Rs. 25,000/- which has been
made before Court below, would stand remitted to the
learned Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, for the settlement
of the dues as directed above.
26. Accordingly, the Appeal from order lacks merit and the
same is hereby dismissed.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
26.04.2022
Mahinder/
